title: Karoo-Ferrar volcanism
summary: Around 183 million years ago during the Early Jurassic, the Karoo-Ferrar large igneous province erupted vast volumes of flood basalt across southern Gondwana, spanning southern Africa and Antarctica. Magma sills intruded organic-rich sedimentary strata, releasing massive quantities of thermogenic greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. This provoked intense global warming and triggered the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event, driving widespread marine deoxygenation and an extinction pulse among marine invertebrates.

uncertainty.note: High-precision radiometric dating places peak Karoo-Ferrar magmatism and carbon release at approximately 183 Ma, coinciding with the early Toarcian oceanic anoxic event (Ruhl et al. 2022; Font et al. 2022).
